subject: Deep ops qualification + SLO summary for NovaPulse
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@novapulse.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — latency/throughput needs & topology notes

Alicia / Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned heading into the deeper ops conversation next week. I wrote this up to capture comms we can use for the internal ops/infra review.

Summary of customer goals / pain:
- Primary goal: real-time scoring for clinical triage suggestions (medical alerts) with 95th-pct latency target <= 200ms for inference at median request size (~256 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state ~400 req/s with 2x burst to 800 req/s during peak events.
- Model: prefer fine-tuned open model family (they mentioned Llama-compat 33B/70B), but open to a smaller distilled variant for peak fallback.
- Constraints: must keep PII in VPC-only flows; audit logging retention 1 year; SOC2 evidence required.

Initial technical read:
- Recommended topology: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with auto-scaling group (buffered min capacity to keep p95 under 200ms). Primary variant: quantized 70B (8-bit) with optimized KV cache. Fallback path: 33B distilled model for degraded latency/cost.
- Batching: dynamic micro-batching with per-customer routing; target batching window <= 10ms to preserve p95.
- Prefix caching: cache common prompt prefixes for triage templates — should reduce token work for repeated templates.

Open questions we need answered from NovaPulse (please confirm / add):
1) Typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95) for their requests — helps sizing KV cache and kernel selection.
2) Acceptable quality vs latency tradeoff: up to how much degradation on long-tail cases is acceptable for fallback model?
3) Any hard procurement constraints (PO lead times, preferred contract terms) that affect Dedicated lead time?

Attachments I'm sending: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft timeline & owner table), slo-topology-diagram.png, and the security questionnaire (partially filled).

Next steps (proposed):
- NovaPulse: share sequence-length histogram + short sample workload (anonymized) by EOD Thu.
- Redwood: ops runbook + cost model for dedicated pool + fallback variant by next Tue (internal: assign to Irene for topology draft).
- Schedule deep ops call w/ infra + security (proposed Wed 07/07 10am PT).

If that matches your notes, I'll push the action items and invite the security folks.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (xlsx), slo-topology-diagram.png (png), security-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Alicia Torres <alicia@novapulse.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Berger <tberger@novapulse.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — latency/throughput needs & topology notes

Connor — thanks, this is exactly the kind of summary we needed. Quick clarifications inline.

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 9:14 AM Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary of customer goals / pain:
> - Primary goal: real-time scoring for clinical triage suggestions (medical alerts) with 95th-pct latency target <= 200ms for inference at median request size (~256 tokens).

Correct: p50 is usually ~120 tokens, p95 is closer to 320 tokens in production (we'll send the histogram). The 200ms p95 is aggressive but feasible if you help with prefix caching + a small warm pool.

> - Throughput: steady-state ~400 req/s with 2x burst to 800 req/s during peak events.

Yes. We have daily micro-bursts around batch job windows, and then larger spikes at the top of the hour for shift changes.

> Open questions we need answered from NovaPulse:
> 1) Typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95) for their requests — helps sizing KV cache and kernel selection.

We'll export the anonymized histograms today and aim to share by EOD.

> 2) Acceptable quality vs latency tradeoff: up to how much degradation on long-tail cases is acceptable for fallback model?

We can tolerate up to ~8% drop in F1 for edge cases at peak only, provided core safety filters remain identical.

> 3) Any hard procurement constraints (PO lead times, preferred contract terms) that affect Dedicated lead time?

Procurement note: PO lead time 4–6 weeks, security attach required (SOC2 + ISO 27001 is ideal). We will need an appendix for data handling in the contract.

Will confirm the histograms and a short anonymized sample by EOD. Also tagging security: we'll add our security lead Tom for the questionnaire.

—Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of Integrations, NovaPulse

---
Quoted attachments from your email acknowledged: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, slo-topology-diagram.png, security-questionnaire.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: internal: ops sizing notes (NovaPulse)

Connor / Lauren — quick internal note after reading the recap and Alicia's reply. Key ops asks I'll take on:
- Produce a cost + latency model for both the 70B quantized primary and 33B fallback. I'll include p95 estimates for 128/256/320 token buckets and the autoscale policies to maintain p95 <= 200ms.
- Topology draft: reserved min pool (N GPUs) + warm buffer nodes in us-west1, multi-variant routing with priority-based fallback, plus a small cross-region failover to us-central in case of AZ outage.
- Security: I'll fill the SOC2 parts of the questionnaire and flag anything requiring Private deployment (VPC-only) — we should confirm whether NovaPulse wants Private or Dedicated.

Questions: can we get a sample of the request rate time-series (15m resolution) instead of per-minute? that helps the autoscaler sim. If Alicia can provide that with histograms we can nail the sizing this week.

I'll draft initial slides and a runbook for the Wed deep ops call.

Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
